title: Debugging with AI
description: Stop staring at stack traces. Learn how to feed errors, logs, and context into AI to pinpoint bugs in seconds.

data.text: Why AI Is Great at Debugging

Debugging is fundamentally a pattern-matching exercise. You have an error message and a body of code, and you need to find where the two do not align. AI models trained on billions of lines of code and thousands of debugging discussions are exceptionally good at this pattern matching, often spotting the root cause in seconds where a human might spend minutes or hours.

The quality of AI debugging help depends almost entirely on the quality of the prompt. A vague "my code is broken" will get a vague response. A structured debugging prompt with error, context, and what you have already tried will get a precise diagnosis.

data.title: Every debugging prompt should include:
items: The full error message and stack trace
The relevant code (the function throwing the error and its dependencies)
What you expected to happen vs. what actually happened
What you have already tried to fix it
The language, framework, and version numbers

data.title: How to approach each:
items: Runtime errors — paste the full stack trace, the line that throws, and the input that caused it
Logic bugs — describe the expected output vs actual output, show the algorithm, ask for the flaw
Performance issues — share a profiler output or timing data, ask where the bottleneck is
Integration bugs — describe the two systems involved, show the integration code and error logs
Test failures — paste the failing test, the code under test, and the assertion error

data.text: Logs are one of the most valuable debugging inputs you can give an AI. Paste the full log output around the error, not just the error line. The lines before the error often contain the root cause — a null value, a missing field, a failed dependency. The AI can cross-reference log patterns with code logic to find the exact problem.

data.title: Sanitize logs before sharing
data.text: Remove or redact any PII, secrets, or sensitive business data from logs before pasting them into a chat interface. The AI does not need your users' real data to understand the bug.

data.title: A practical workflow:
items: Paste the error and context. Ask the AI for the likely cause.
Implement the suggested fix. Run the code.
If the error changes, paste the new error and what you changed.
Repeat until the bug is resolved.
Once resolved, ask the AI to explain why the bug occurred — this builds your mental model

data.title: Debugging limitations to be aware of:
items: The AI can only diagnose what you show it — if you omit the relevant code, the diagnosis will be wrong
It may suggest a fix that works but is not idiomatic to your codebase
It may confidently assert a cause that is plausible but incorrect — always verify
It cannot run your code or inspect your runtime environment directly

data.title: Effective debugging prompt
Always verify the fix
data.text: After applying an AI-suggested fix, run your tests and verify the fix actually resolves the issue. AI debugging is a powerful starting point, but the final verification must be done by running the code.

data.title: Debugging with AI
points: Include the full error, relevant code, and what you expected
Share logs around the error, not just the error line
Iterate: apply the fix, run, share the new error if it changes
Sanitize logs to remove secrets and PII
Always verify the final fix by running your code
